Not recommended – very poor experience
I took admission in April 2023 at Walk In Institute, Dadar branch for a 1-year Diploma in Fine Arts.At the time of enquiry, the receptionist Akshanka Kotian informed me and my parents that:
The course is 1 year
3 days online (1 hour) and 3 days offline (2 hours)
Final exam would be a government MCQ-based exam

However, online classes never started, despite repeatedly asking. Because of this, it became clear that the course could not be completed within 1 year, which was a false promise.
Later, the Fine Arts teacher Pranalika Pawar stated that the final exam is a written theory exam, not MCQ, which completely contradicted what was told during admission.
I completed around 150 lectures and submitted all monthly assignments on time, but the teacher imposed her own rules, such as compulsory attendance and demanding extra assignments every Sunday. Her behavior was rude, forceful, and mentally stressful.
In February 2024, I had a serious hand/medical issue. Instead of understanding, I was pressurized continuously, which affected my health and mental peace. Art education should be supportive, not stressful.
In April 2024, I submitted a written medical letter, yet the institute remained insensitive.
When I requested a refund in June 2024, I was told clearly:No refund in any case, even if you come with a politician.”
This response reflects their unprofessional and unethical attitude.
After receiving full fees, their behavior completely changed. I genuinely felt the institute is only money-oriented, not student-oriented. The teacher also made disrespectful comments about reputed colleges, which was highly unprofessional.I even paid ₹5,000 regeneration fees in April 2023, despite already paying the full course amount earlier.This institute lacks transparency, professionalism, empathy, and student support. Promises made during admission are not fulfilled.

I am sharing my personal experience so think before joining.
